complete_examples.text: The Hermitian cubic interpolation polynomial is used as shape function of the Bernoulli–Euler beam.
The rail, slab and concrete supporting layer (CSL) are all modeled by a uniform Bernoulli–Euler beam.

The rails are modelled as spatial Bernoulli–Euler beam supported by discrete viscoelastic supports with finite length under the condition that the effects of boundary conditions can be ignored, and rail pads are assumed as linear spring elements and damper elements.
The rail is regarded as Bernoulli–Euler beam supported by discrete viscoelastic supports, and rail pads are assumed as linear spring elements and linear damper elements.
The rails are modeled as Bernoulli–Euler beam with the consideration of its nodal displacements and rotations toward the X-, Y- and Z-axes.
The track subsystem mainly includes the rail represented by Bernoulli–Euler beam and the track slabs represented by Mindlin plates.
According to the investigations [37], the Bernoulli–Euler beam is accurately enough to simulate rail dynamic behaviour within pin-pin frequency point.
The sleeper is modelled as a Bernoulli–Euler beam for its vertical and longitudinal motions, but regarded as linear axial deformation for its lateral motion.
The rail is modeled as a Bernoulli–Euler beam, the track slab and concrete basement are modeled as an assemblage of thin-plate elements.
